response:
Diagnosis before proposing:

Generation 4 produced the two best signals in the archive and they come from *different* channels:
- **HierarchicalProfitRestraint** (fmb 3.60, alpha 3.8%, t 3.67, Sharpe 0.46, coverage 0.122) confirmed that the COALESCE profitability hierarchy fixes the coverage/alpha trade-off: it beat both the oancf-only (4.2% but coverage 0.082, t only 2.67) and oibdp-only (2.9%) versions on every statistic that matters. Own-history capex restraint remains the right investment leg.
- **ProfitableIntangibleTilt** (fmb 4.18, alpha 3.6%, t 3.23, coverage 0.133) confirmed my read of the earlier sign reversal: investment *composition* is a second, independent mechanism — profitable firms whose spending is research-tilted are underpriced because expensing understates their earning power. Its low Sharpe (0.29) versus the restraint family (0.46–0.56) suggests it is a distinct, noisier but additive source of alpha.
- Diminishing channels: MaintenanceCapexCashCow (capx/dp) gave only 1.4%, so depreciation-based benchmarking is inferior to own-history percentiles; ProfitAccelVsCapexDecel (1.7%, t 1.92) shows second differences are weaker than first-order trends, so the trend-divergence family should stay at the slope level.

Priority now is consolidation: (a) merge the restraint and composition channels, (b) resolve whether cash-flow profitability also improves the trend-divergence signal, (c) test one new benchmarking dimension (industry-relative restraint) and one new quality dimension (accrual-based earnings quality interacted with restraint), and (d) repair the weak FMB slope of the cumulative-payoff channel.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: HarvestAndIntangibleTilt
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), SUMRANK(NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Underpriced cash generators are profitable firms that both hold physical reinvestment below their own historical norm and direct the spending they do undertake toward research rather than capacity; the two forms of investment discipline are complementary and should compound.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's two strongest signals isolate different investment legs — own-history restraint (Sharpe 0.46–0.56) and research tilt (fmb 4.18) — while sharing the same profitability channel, so merging them tests additivity rather than restating either. The COALESCE profitability hierarchy is retained because it demonstrably raised alpha, t-stat, and coverage simultaneously in generation 4.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: ResearchStockVsPhysicalStock
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ppegt), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters for mismeasured earning power is the accumulated stock of research capital relative to installed physical capital, not the single-year spending mix; profitable firms whose economic capital is mostly unbooked research are the most underpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: ProfitableIntangibleTilt used a one-year flow share and delivered a strong FMB slope but a modest Sharpe, consistent with a noisy annual mix measure; cumulating five years of R&D into a stock and benchmarking it against gross PP&E should stabilize portfolio composition. This isolates the flow-versus-stock design choice inside the composition channel rather than duplicating it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CashProfitTrendVsCapexTrend
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(TREND(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(oibdp, at)), 5)), RANK(TREND(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose cash profitability is trending up while their reinvestment rate trends down are transitioning to harvest, and cash-based profitability tracks that transition more faithfully than accrual operating income.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: MarginTrendVsCapexTrend still holds the archive's most precise alpha (3.6%, t 3.71) using accrual operating profitability, while the cash-flow hierarchy lifted every statistic in the restraint family; this applies that one proven substitution to the trend family. It is a deliberate single-design-choice test whose outcome tells us whether the cash-flow advantage is general or specific to level-based restraint measures.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: IndustryRelativeRestraintCashCow
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(COALESCE(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 3), MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3))), RANK(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(capx, ppent))))
HYPOTHESIS: Investment norms are set by technology within an industry, so a profitable firm spending well below its industry's reinvestment norm is exercising genuine discipline, whereas a low absolute capex rate may merely reflect an asset-light industry.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Own-history conditioning succeeded because it escaped the cross-sectional low-investment direction that CMA already prices; industry-relative conditioning is the other natural way to strip out permanent capital-intensity differences, and it applies to firms without long histories. Comparing it head-to-head with the TS_RANK version identifies which benchmark carries the harvesting information.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: EarningsQualityAndCapexRestraint
EXPRESSION: SUB(RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at))), RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose earnings are fully backed by cash and that are simultaneously restraining reinvestment relative to their own history are true cash generators; firms with accrual-inflated earnings that keep spending are the ones the market credits for both quality and growth it will not receive.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This replaces the profitability *level* leg with an earnings *quality* leg, a distinct economic dimension that explains why cash-flow profitability outperformed accrual profitability throughout the archive rather than just exploiting it. Because the accrual gap is nearly orthogonal to the RMW profitability level, the interaction should not be absorbed by FF5 in the way the earlier level composites were.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: RealizedPayoffPlusProfitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3), WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(oiadp, 3), TS_SUM(capx, 3)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are both persistently profitable and can show that their last three years of capital spending actually produced incremental operating profit have demonstrated value-creating investment, whereas persistent profitability with no payoff on cumulative spending signals capital destruction.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The cumulative-payoff ratio produced a reliable FF5 alpha (2.8%, t 2.97) but almost no Fama-MacBeth slope (1.24), the signature of a tail-driven measure; anchoring it with a smooth profitability level should supply the missing cross-sectional monotonicity while preserving the payoff-realization economics. This repairs the specific failure mode of that channel instead of discarding it.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
